### J-1 Compose and fix check "as today" have no artefact to version and no way to close a finding that became a fix task
- quote: "`compose(led, current)`, as today"
- quote: "a version no juror has judged is never approved"
- quote: "The findings a lens gives a fix verdict on in a re-review (#52 FR-7, FR-9): its own, disposed as fixed."
- quote: "if gate not in GATES:"
- quote: "a re-review is a fix check of the lens's findings"
- situation (architecture-fit): Today `compose` compares a blob of `artefact(root, slug, gate)`, built from the files in `GATES`, against the round's version. `fixcheck` diffs the items of that same text. No contract gives `implementation-E-n` a `GATES` entry or says what `current` is at this gate. If it is the spec files, a code fix changes nothing and `fixcheck` shows nothing changed. If it includes `tasks.md`, each append makes the round stale. Separately, `pack_ids` returns only findings with status `disposed` and a disposition in `FIXES`, and CT-14 never says what status or disposition a finding gets once its task is appended. If findings stay `open`, the re-review pack is empty, `compose` sees them as unresolved and they can never get a `fixed` verdict, so AC-40 and TC-58 cannot pass with `compose` and `pack_ids` unchanged.
- fix: State in CT-13 or CT-9 what this gate's version is (for example the epic's last commit) and how `fixcheck` shows the change (the diff since the judged commit). State in CT-14 the finding's transition when its task is appended, with the disposition it takes in `DISPOSITIONS` and `FIXES`.
- validation: confirmed: CT-13 says `compose(led, current)` "as today", but `artefact()` indexes `GATES[gate]`, which has no `implementation-E-n` entry. No contract says what `current` is, or what status or disposition a finding takes once CT-14 appends its task. `pack_ids` returns only findings that are `disposed` with a `FIXES` disposition, so AC-40 and TC-58 cannot pass.
- disposition: plan-fix by agent: CT-13: current is the epic's last commit; CT-9 fix check diffs from the judged commit; CT-14 fix-task disposition

### J-2 CT-12 reuses `evidence` for a file or area, but the field already means observed or inferred, and the binding misses the quote check
- quote: "Fails: no gap, cite or evidence → `INVALID` naming the field"
- quote: "its evidence as a file or area"
- quote: "`evidence` observed or inferred"
- quote: "Whitespace-insensitive for quotes."
- quote: "a cited ID or quote is not in the artefact"
- situation (architecture-fit): `parse_lens` rejects any `evidence` value outside observed and inferred, and `compose` depends on the inferred-can't-block rule. CT-12's shape adds only `gap` and `run`, so a finding has nowhere to name the file or area that FR-21 and TC-35 require. A value such as `src/x.py` is `INVALID`, and `observed` satisfies the field without naming a file. CT-12 also binds only `parse_lens`, but the word-for-word check is in `grounded`, called from `add`, and `add` writes one fixed reason, while AC-29 needs the reason to name FR-99. Changing `parse_lens` alone leaves AC-30 and AC-29 failing.
- fix: Add a separate field such as `- where: <file or area>` to CT-12's shape and leave `evidence` as it is. Also bind `grounded` and `add`: skip quote matching at this gate, and make the drop reason name the undefined ID.
- validation: confirmed: `parse_lens` rejects any `evidence` value outside `{observed, inferred}`, yet FR-21 wants "evidence as a file or area" and CT-12's shape adds only `gap` and `run`. The word-for-word quote check is in `grounded`, called from `add`, which writes one fixed reason ("a cited ID or quote is not in the artefact"). AC-29 needs the reason to name FR-99, and CT-12 binds only `parse_lens`.
- disposition: plan-fix by agent: CT-12: separate where field; evidence keeps its meaning; grounded and add bound

### J-4 A finding doesn't carry what routing and a valid fix task need
- quote: "Returns: a task under the epic's `#### Fixes`, the next free ID, `From: J-n (implementation-E-n, round n)`; unrequested says justify or remove."
- quote: "on a full spec `Test:` cites the plan's `TC-n`"
- quote: "card: nio-worker-{task['tier']}"
- quote: "Accepts: a contradicts finding where the code is the right side"
- quote: "| contradicts | code | change request; the spec is not edited | [human] |"
- situation (architecture-fit): `tasks.check` requires `Files`, `Serves`, `Test`, `Depends on`, `Parallel`, `Tier`, `Effort` and `Mode` on every task, fix tasks included, and on a full spec `Test` must cite a `TC-n`. CT-14 gives only the heading and `From:`, and `append_fix` takes only the epic and the finding, which has no files, tier or test. A generated task would then fail `nio check tasks`, and with no `Tier` `claim` would print the card `nio-worker-`. A missing-test finding may also have no existing `TC-n` to cite. Routing has the same hole: the decision table splits `contradicts` by right side, but CT-12 adds no such field and no contract says who decides it, although `nio jury check --record` routes findings on its own (architecture.md).
- situation (logic): a conformance lens reports `gap: contradicts`.
- fix: Have CT-14 state how each required field is derived or defaulted, including `Test` when no `TC-n` fits, and how the check accepts it. Add a right-side field to the finding format, or name who sets it before `--record` routes the finding.
- validation: confirmed: `tasks.check` requires `Files`, `Serves`, `Test`, `Depends on`, `Parallel`, `Tier`, `Effort` and `Mode` on fix tasks too, and on a full spec `Test` must cite a `TC-n`. CT-14 gives only the heading and `From:`, and `append_fix` takes only the epic and the finding. The decision table's `contradicts` split by right side has no field in CT-12.
- disposition: plan-fix by grill: Grill Q26: reviewer states right, unset means spec; CT-12; CT-14 states each task field

### J-5 CT-17 moves the `epic` line out of `epic_end` but doesn't say who writes it or the stage-ending `pass` line
- quote: "`epic_end` no longer writes `skipped: not built`"
- quote: "Returns: the `epic` line is written when the gate is approved or closed; its `reason` is the outcome"
- quote: "`pass` line implementing -> done"
- quote: "only `nio flow` writes `state.json` and `history.jsonl`; never edit them"
- quote: "`nio jury check --record` on this gate also appends the fix tasks and writes change requests (FR-26, FR-30)."
- situation (architecture-fit): Today `epic_end` runs inside a `T-n:` commit and writes the `epic` line and, after the last epic, the `pass` line, with both committed by `commit`. Under CT-17 no `epic` line exists when the last task finishes, so `shut` never covers the epic and `pass` is never written there. No contract names the command that writes the two lines at approval, or the commit that carries them. The natural place is `nio jury check --record`, which would make `jury` write flow history, against the rule that only `nio flow` does. The effort could then stay at implementing after the last gate is approved. The report's `merge:` line and its "skipped" `notify:` line depend on the same code and are also unassigned.
- situation (logic): the last epic of the effort finishes its last task.
- situation (risk-rollback): Today `epic_end` writes the `pass` line and prints `merge:` in the same call, inside the last task's commit. CT-17 moves only the `epic` line and is silent on `pass`. If `epic_end` keeps its current logic, which adds the current epic to `shut`, the last epic's final task moves the effort to done and tells the human to merge before its gate has run. A rejection then has to send a done effort back to implementing, and the `pass` line can't be taken back from the history. If `pass` is dropped from `epic_end` instead, no contract writes it and the effort stays in implementing. No test covers the gate on the last epic.
- fix: Have CT-17 name the `nio flow` command that writes the `epic` line and, after the last epic, the `pass` line, say which commit carries them, and say what `epic_end`'s report prints instead.
- validation: confirmed: `epic_end` in `implement.py` currently writes both the `epic` line and the `pass` line, inside the `T-n:` commit. CT-17 says the `epic` line is written at approval or close but names no writer, and does not mention the `pass` line or the `merge:` report. Only `nio flow` may write history, and `jury check --record` is the only candidate hook in the plan.
- disposition: plan-fix by agent: CT-17: nio flow done implementation-E-n writes epic and, after the last epic, pass and merge; epic_end writes neither

### J-11 The throwaway copy shares the human's git data, and nothing proves it is removed
- quote: "a detached `git worktree` at the epic's last commit, removed after the runs"
- quote: "the human's working tree is byte-for-byte unchanged after the run"
- quote: "the worktree can't be created → ValueError naming git's error, and nothing runs"
- situation (risk-rollback): A linked worktree shares refs, hooks, config and objects with the human's `.git`. A test or attack that runs `git branch -D`, `git update-ref` or `git config` in the copy changes the human's repo for good, and TC-41 only compares the working tree, so it would still pass. Separately, a run that leaves files behind makes a plain `git worktree remove` fail, and a killed `nio jury evidence` leaves the worktree and its admin entry behind. CT-2 doesn't say how the removal handles a dirty copy, where the copy lives, or how the next run clears a stale one. That change to the human's refs can't be undone from the plan, and the leftovers pile up unnoticed.
- fix: Make the copy not share `.git` (for example a `git archive` export or a standalone clone at the commit), or state why a worktree is safe. Add to CT-2 a forced removal in a `finally` and a stale-copy cleanup on the next start. Extend TC-41 so the test also runs git commands, and assert that refs, config and `git worktree list` are unchanged after a normal run and after a timeout.
- validation: confirmed: architecture.md and CT-2 use a detached `git worktree`, which shares refs, config and objects with the human's `.git`. TC-41 and AC-53 only compare the working tree. CT-2 says nothing about forced removal, a dirty copy, or clearing a stale worktree after a killed run.
- disposition: plan-fix by grill: Grill Q27, 'Local clone': CT-2, architecture.md, TC-41 extended

### J-12 Running the record step twice raises a second change request for the same finding
- quote: "a pending change record against the spec; spec.md is unchanged"
- quote: "`None` when the finding already has a task"
- quote: "`nio jury check --record` on this gate also appends the fix tasks and writes change requests"
- quote: "spec.md is byte-for-byte unchanged and one pending change request cites the finding"
- situation (risk-rollback): CT-14 defines a no-op on repeat, but CT-15 has no such rule. `jury.check` saves the ledger only at its end, so a stop after `raise_change` leaves no mark that the request was raised. The next `--record` writes another permanent record under `.nio/memory/`. FR-44 holds the epic until the human rules on each request, so the human rules twice and can accept one and reject the other for the same finding. TC-65 and TC-54 run the step once. TC-64 runs it twice, but only for an unrequested finding.
- fix: Give `raise_change` the same rule as `append_fix`: return the existing record when a change record already cites this finding, and store the link so it survives a stop before the ledger save. Add a test that runs `nio jury check --record` twice on a contradicts finding, and once more after a simulated stop before the save, and asserts one change record.
- validation: confirmed: CT-14 has a no-op rule (`None` when the finding already has a task), but CT-15's `raise_change` has none. `jury.check` saves the ledger only at its end. A second `--record` can therefore write another change record, and TC-54, TC-64 and TC-65 never run a contradicts finding twice.
- disposition: plan-fix by agent: CT-15: a repeat returns the existing record; TC-71

### J-13 Existing `skipped: not built` epic lines have no migration rule, and rolling back leaves an epic stuck
- quote: "`epic_end` no longer writes `skipped: not built`"
- quote: "`nio flow claim` refuses the next epic until the `epic` line exists"
- quote: "`left` and `epic_end` keep reading it."
- situation (risk-rollback): `epic` lines live in the append-only history, and `left` and the planned claim check only test whether a line exists, not its `reason`. An effort mid-implementation at upgrade time has E-1 marked `skipped: not built`, so it counts as closed: the new gate never runs on it and nobody is told. In the other direction, an epic finished under new code has no line until its gate ends. If the code is rolled back, old `epic_end` only fires when a task of that epic commits, so `left` reports `E-n has no epic line` indefinitely and the stage guard can't pass. Those history lines can't be edited, because only `nio flow` writes them. The plan names no recovery path and no test uses an old line.
- fix: State in CT-17 what an existing `skipped: not built` line means after the upgrade: either it stays closed and is reported to the human, or the gate may be run on that epic and a later `epic` line supersedes it. Say how a rollback recovers an epic with no line. Add a test with a history holding an old `skipped: not built` line, covering `flow next`, `claim` and `left`.
- validation: confirmed: `left` and the claim check only test that an `epic` line exists, not its `reason`. CT-17 and architecture.md do not say what an existing `skipped: not built` line means after the change, and no test uses one. The implement stage has just shipped, so such efforts are plausible.
- disposition: plan-fix by grill: Grill Q28, 'Stay closed, say so': CT-17; TC-70

### J-15 No contract commits the fix tasks, ledger or `epic` line, so they exist only in the working tree
- quote: "so the committed ledger stands alone"
- quote: "`.nio/specs/<slug>/tasks.md`: fix tasks are appended under the epic's `#### Fixes`"

- situation (risk-rollback): `implement.commit` stages only paths outside the effort folder, plus `history.jsonl` and `state.json`. Appended fix tasks in `tasks.md` and `jury/implementation-E-n.json` and `.md` are therefore never staged by a task commit. CT-14, CT-16, CT-17 and CT-19 name no commit either, and the skill's approval commits cover only the plan and tasks gates. The findings, and the `From:` lines that stop a second append, could stay uncommitted across rounds or be lost at merge or in a clean checkout. Losing them erases the gate's only record of why fix tasks exist, and the "committed ledger" architecture.md relies on may not exist. Inserting into a middle epic's section also rewrites the whole of `tasks.md`, and no contract requires that write to be atomic, so a stop mid-write could cut off uncommitted fix tasks.

Require `append_fix` to write through a temporary file and rename. Add a test asserting that after a rejected outcome those paths are in `git log` and `git status` is clean for them.

The appended `tasks.md` edits and `jury/implementation-E-n.*` are therefore never staged. The jury SKILL.md commits only `nio: approve plan` and `nio: approve tasks`, and CT-14, CT-16, CT-17 and CT-19 name no commit for this gate.
- disposition: plan-fix by agent: CT-17: each recorded outcome is committed through flow.commit_gate; CT-14 atomic write; TC-72

None can go green in its own entry, so a worker working in order hits a failing test it can't fix, and the failures look like attempts rather than a plan fault.
- fix: move each TC to the first story that delivers everything it covers, and add the contracts it really needs to `Covers:`. TC-1 goes to US-3 or later, or its assert is cut to what CT-1 delivers.
- validation: confirmed: plan.md lists TC-1 under US-1, but its assert needs the CT-8 plan (US-3) and the CT-10 cards (US-7), and TC-1 covers CT-19 (US-6). TC-5, TC-6 and TC-13 sit in US-2 but cover CT-12 (US-5). TC-38, TC-44, TC-46 and TC-47 sit in US-5 but need CT-14 or CT-15 (US-6), and TC-24 sits in US-3 but needs the verdict in CT-16 (US-6).
- disposition: plan-fix by agent: Tests moved to the first story that delivers what they cover; Covers lines corrected

### J-17 TC-56 expects `human`, but compose as today gives `approved` for a lone new major
- quote: "- Assert: outcome `human`; the new major is shown as a note."
- quote: "- Shape: `compose(led, current)`, as today"
- quote: "g.update(status="noted", validation="grounded", reason="raised in a re-review below blocker: a note only")"
- quote: "return "approved", [], []"
- situation (test-proof): in a re-review, `add` marks a new major `noted`. `compose` lists only `open` findings as unresolved, so with nothing else open it returns approved. Either the test fails against the contract as written, or the fixture holds an older open finding the setup doesn't mention. In that case `human` comes from that finding and the test proves nothing about the new major. The bug it lets through is a silent approval over a new major.
- fix: settle which behaviour AC-38 means. If the fixture needs another open finding, say so in the setup. If a lone noted major must give `human`, that contradicts "unchanged" in FR-32 and goes to the spec as a change request.
- validation: confirmed: In a re-review `add` sets a new major to `noted`, and `compose` counts only `open` findings as unresolved. With nothing else open it returns `approved`, not the `human` that AC-38 and TC-56 expect. CT-13 says "as today", so the test fails unless the fixture hides an older open finding.
- disposition: spec-change by human: C-261030-fohc: Grill Q29, 'Comes to you': FR-32 gains the exception; TC-56 asserts human with nothing else open

### J-18 The evidence tests can pass by echoing the fixed lens output; no contract joins a lens's match to the run results
- quote: "- Assert: two entries, each with the AC ID, a `file:line` and `passed`, while the tests' source holds no AC IDs; the lens's own matching is judged by the lens card's evaluation, not this test."
- quote: "- Accepts: written only by CT-3 and CT-11"
- quote: "- Setup: an AC the epic covers has no test, and a fixed conformance lens output saying so"
- quote: "- Assert: one missing-evidence finding per AC of the epic; the crash output is in the results."
- quote: "- Assert: a no-assertion hint naming the test in every lens pack; the AC ends with a missing-evidence finding."
- quote: "- Returns: one hint per stub, uncertain reference, no-assertion test, and changed or removed assertion line; hints never enter the ledger"
- situation (test-proof): CT-7's shape has no per-AC entry and nothing at collect writes one. CT-12 only parses findings, so nothing checks a lens's match against the FR-3 result. If the fixtures already hold the finding, TC-5, TC-6, TC-18 and TC-39 pass while collect does nothing but parse. A lens that matches a failed or no-assertion test, or calls a missing test minor, gets through. If the fixtures hold only a match, TC-6 and TC-39 can't pass, because no contract creates the finding. TC-4's fixtures are all passing, so `passed` copied from the lens passes too. TC-14 also expects a correctness entry when "the gate starts", with no lens run and no format for such an entry.
- fix: add a contract for the step that reads a lens's AC-to-test match, takes `file:line` and the result from `results.json`, and writes the missing-evidence finding at blocker itself. Have the fixtures state only the match. Add a TC-4 variant where the lens claims `passed` for a failing test. Define the correctness entry on a flag, and run TC-14 from a fixed lens output.
- validation: confirmed: CT-7's schema has no per-AC entries, yet TC-4 asserts "two entries, each with the AC ID, a file:line and passed". Nothing in CT-12 or CT-3 joins a lens's AC-to-test match to the `results.json` results, so TC-5 and TC-6 only prove that `parse_lens` parses a fixed output. TC-14 also expects a correctness-lens entry at "the gate starts" with no lens run.
- disposition: plan-fix by agent: CT-21 joins matches to results; fixtures hold only matches; TC-73; TC-14 runs from a fixed output

### J-19 The human's pick has no contract, and TC-23 and TC-66 can't catch a lens dropped without it
- quote: "- Assert: the plan output lists 5 runs, each with its tier, and the choices run all or pick (no hit rates recorded yet); no lens output is collected before a pick."
- quote: "- Shape: `nio jury plan <slug> implementation-E-n`"
- quote: "- Setup: `jury.max_runs` set to 4, a plan of 5 runs, and the human picks a set without one triggered lens"
- quote: "- Assert: the outcome is not approved, and it names the missing lens"
- quote: "missing = [lens for lens in led["expect"] if lens not in lenses]"
- situation (test-proof): TC-23's action is only planning, so "no lens output is collected" holds whatever collect does. Nothing in the contracts records a pick, so TC-24 has nothing to call and no ledger field to read when naming dropped lenses. TC-66 passes on the existing `expect` check if the fixture expects all 5. If the agent passes only 4 `--expect` flags, it approves. So the misuse the test is named for, an agent dropping a lens on its own, isn't caught.
- fix: give the pick a contract (command, record, and collect refusing lens outputs over the cap without one). Make TC-23 try a collect before the pick and assert refusal. Make TC-66 use the agent's own 4 `--expect` values, not 5.
- validation: confirmed: CT-8 says no lens is collected "before a pick", but no contract defines the pick command, its record, or a collect refusal. TC-23 only plans, and TC-66 relies on the existing `led["expect"]` check, which passes if the agent passes only 4 `--expect` flags. TC-24 has no ledger field to read when naming dropped lenses.
- disposition: plan-fix by agent: CT-8: --pick records picked and dropped, collect refuses without it; TC-23, TC-24, TC-66

### J-21 A CLI finding that became a fix task has no lens to verify it, and a repeat is swallowed
- quote: "ledger entries with lens `cli`, kind `gap`, validation `confirmed`, never in a refuter batch and never a vote; a repeat with the same title adds none"
- situation (architecture-fit): CT-14 marks a finding `disposed` with `fix-task` "so its lens gets a fix verdict". For a CT-20 finding that lens is `cli`, and `cli` is not a planned lens, has no card and gets no pack, so no juror can give that verdict. This covers phantom completion, tampering, failed lint or type checks and, through CT-21, every missing-evidence blocker. When evidence runs again after the fix task and the same check still fails, CT-20's "a repeat with the same title adds none" adds nothing and leaves the entry `disposed`. No contract says a clean re-run closes the finding or that a repeat reopens it. So a fix task that did not fix a failing test has two possible outcomes: compose waits forever for a verdict nobody can give, or it treats the finding as settled and approves an epic with a test still failing, against FR-5 and FR-6. TC-68 runs the repeat only with the finding still open. TC-58 asserts "each lens pack is a fix check of its findings", which says nothing about `cli` findings.
- fix: State in CT-20 how a `fix-task` CLI finding is closed, with a CLI verdict and no juror. When `nio jury evidence` or `join` re-checks, a finding that no longer recurs is marked fixed, and one that recurs goes back to open, or is reported as not fixed, under the same J-n. Say in CT-13 that `cli` findings need no juror's fix verdict and that an unfixed one counts as unresolved. Add a test where the fix task leaves the check failing and the epic is not approved.
- validation: confirmed: CT-14 sets a fix-task finding to `disposed`, and `pack_ids` returns a finding only to a lens named in its `sources`. A CT-20 finding's only source lens is `cli`, which has no pack, so no juror can rule on it. CT-20 says "a repeat with the same title adds none" and no contract covers the re-check. `compose` counts only `open` findings, so a fix task that left the check failing can still be approved. TC-68 and TC-58 do not cover this case.
- disposition: plan-fix by agent: CT-20: the CLI gives the fix verdict on its own findings at the next evidence run; a repeat is not fixed, same J-n, no second task; CT-13 counts it unresolved; TC-75
